content:
After WhatsApp first introduced Liquid Glass earlier this year on iOS, the app is now working to bring the design to more interface elements. Here's what you need to know.

Liquid Glass is coming to the WhatsApp drawing editor and video player

If this feels familiar, bear with us: WhatsApp is expanding its Liquid Glass redesign to more parts of the app.

Earlier this year, WhatsApp finally rolled out its first wave of Liquid Glass changes more broadly after more than six months of testing.

At the time, WhatsApp's parent company was also working to bring the new design to elements like the voice message player, message reactions, and contextual menus, though those changes remained limited to beta versions of the app.

According to WABetaInfo, the latest WhatsApp iOS beta shows that the company is preparing to extend Liquid Glass visuals to more interface elements, including the drawing editor and the video player's progress bar.

WABetaInfo reports:

It's worth noting that some 9to5Mac readers have regularly expressed that their iPhones still haven't received the first wave of Liquid Glass updates; however, this news shows that Meta is continuing to adopt the new visual language, not only on iOS, but also on macOS and iPadOS.

Back to the news at hand, WABetaInfo notes: "This feature is still in development and not yet available for beta users to try out."
